text:
Sometimes I feel my blood running in waves,

just like a fountain of rhythmic sobs;

I hear it run in long murmurs,

but in vain I feel myself to find the wound.


Through the city, like a closed field,

it goes transforming stones into islets,

slaking the thirst of every creature,

and coloring all nature red.


Often I have asked these wines

to calm for a single day the terror that gnaws me;

wine makes the gaze clearer and the ear keener.


I have sought in love a dream of oblivion;

but for me love is a prickling bed,

made to give those cruel women drink.

translation.title: The Fountain of Blood
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the unlocated wound, the city flooded with blood, and the failed consolations of wine and love.
